Elena R: build/linkcheck failing on the docsite, looks like anchors created from headings with ellipses are inconsistent across mkdocs/docusaurus. see build: https://ci.example.com/reds/9876 Elena R: failing error: \"Broken anchor: #examples…\" (note the ellipsis char) Elena R: snippet from docs/usage/quickstart.md: ```markdown ### Examples… Short examples and snippets ``` Ravi S: ah yep, unicode ellipsis (U+2026) vs three dots is the usual culprit. some slugifiers normalize differently between mkdocs and docusaurus. Maggie L: quick grep to find these: `rg \"^#{1,6}\\s+.*\\.\\.\\.\" docs/ -n` will show headings that literally have three dots, but for the ellipsis char use `rg \"\\u2026\" docs/ -n` Tom K: could also be emojis or inline code interfering (e.g., `### Examples :sparkles:` renders anchor with `examples-sparkles` in one and `examples-` in another) Elena R: what's the best short fix? we have a small batch of pages with these headings and a failing nightly linkcheck job. Ravi S: options: - normalize headings in source (replace ellipsis with `...` or remove) - add explicit html anchors: `

Examples…

` (works but noisy) - add frontmatter `slug` per page for deterministic path (good for big pages) Maggie L: i'll open a tiny PR that normalizes unicode ellipsis -> three ascii dots and strips trailing punctuation in headings. quick patch: ```bash # run in repo root python - <<'PY' import pathlib,re for p in pathlib.Path('docs').rglob('*.md'): s=p.read_text(encoding='utf8') s2=re.sub('\\u2026', '...', s) s2=re.sub('(#+\\s+.+?)\\s+[.]{3,}\\n', '\\1\\n', s2) if s2!=s: p.write_text(s2, encoding='utf8') print('fixed', p) PY ``` Ravi S: nice, keep it minimal. we should also add a check in linkcheck that normalizes anchors before comparing, filed an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/459 Elena R: Maggie can you include a changelog entry and target the `docs-linkfix` branch? Maggie L: opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/8423 with the cleanup + tests. marking as draft for now. Tom K: I'll review and add a tiny unit test for our slugifier: assert slug(\"Examples…\") == \"examples\" and slug(\"Examples :sparkles:\") == \"examples-sparkles\" Elena R: CI showed linkcheck failing before, retested against branch? ci-bot: CI job docs/linkcheck (pull/8423) queued ci-bot: docs/linkcheck (pull/8423) failed — diff shows 4 anchors still mismatched, see logs: https://ci.example.com/reds/9876/logs/452 Maggie L: looking at logs — two remaining are generated from codeblock headings inside README includes. those get transformed by the include plugin and preserve ascii/ellipses weirdly. I'll add normalization in the include preprocessor. Maggie L: pushed new commit to PR (force-push) with include-normalize fix ci-bot: docs/linkcheck (pull/8423) passed :white_check_mark: Elena R: awesome — can we also add a short note in CONTRIBUTING.md to avoid Unicode punctuation in headings? small PR followup ok. Ravi S: +1, and we should add an entry to the nightly monitoring playbook: if >3 anchor failures in linkcheck, auto-open a tracking issue and notify #docs. Tom K: merged PR 8423 and added slug tests, thanks team :rocket: Elena R: thanks all — leaving a follow-up issue for frontmatter `slug` fallback for heavy pages: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/460 Maggie L: noted, will schedule next-week triage to decide pages to pin. Elena R: closing the loop — nightly linkcheck green now. :tada:
